title: Machine learning predicts pulmonary Long Covid sequelae using clinical data.
summary: The open-access primary article evaluates three AI approaches for pulmonary Long-Covid sequelae from clinical features and reports multimodality classifier selection with cross-validated performance; the result is a bounded clinical prediction study.
ai_technology: Three ML approaches predict pulmonary sequelae from COVID-positive patient clinical features.
organization: Unit of Computer Systems and Bioinformatics, Department of Engineering, University Campus Bio-Medico of Rome, Via Alvaro del Portillo 21, Rome, 00128, Italy

evidence.tested: The open-access primary article evaluates three AI approaches for pulmonary Long-Covid sequelae from clinical features and reports multimodality classifier selection with cross-validated performance; the result is a bounded clinical prediction study.
evidence.unknown: Results are limited to the reported models, cohorts, datasets or experiments; broader generalization and clinical or operational benefit were not established.
